title: W06a: reconciliation CLI and MCP surfaces with worker context
description: Expose reconciliation with identical semantics on both surfaces: CLI git reconcile with --commit, --agent, optional --repo, --task, --close and --json; MCP reconcile_git_commit with commit, agent, repo, task, close and worker_context. The actor is required and nonempty and identifies the Waystation actor, not the Git author. MCP keeps its fixed ledger root; in adapter mode it validates worker_context (binding_id, binding_generation, expected_ledger_root, caller_worktree) before mutation, verifies that the expected ledger matches its fixed root, and resolves a request-local caller context. A launch option for adapter-configured servers requires that context for worker mutations and Git-context-dependent reads while direct clients keep existing startup defaults. CLI failures return nonzero status with a valid JSON envelope when JSON is requested, including argument errors, and neither surface emits raw stacks or transport-specific task-source values. Implementation baseline: merged main 6276d5f / ledger closure e64d4bd, Waystation 0.6.0 on Bun 1.4.1; see docs/reconciliation-2026-09-27.md. Reuse the merged foundation and its tests. Reuse captureInvocationContext/resolveEvidenceSource rather than changing process cwd/environment. This task owns shared CLI/MCP adapter-mode context plumbing; later W06 wrappers reuse it. Do not expose close until W04c's reopened-work guard is complete.
acceptance: CLI help, JSON output and exit codes, and MCP tool schemas cover every documented field, and both surfaces return equivalent results for the same input.
A missing or contradictory worker context is refused before any mutation, and a request context naming another ledger root is refused.
Direct MCP clients keep existing startup defaults, and concurrent requests with different caller worktrees do not interfere.
Existing claim, finish, status and attachment behavior and legacy defaults are unchanged.
Human output distinguishes attachment, closure with attachment, closure using existing evidence and no_change; JSON argument errors remain valid envelopes with nonzero CLI exit status.
notes: Acceptance group A11. The MCP claim surface currently accepts only an id and an agent, so per-call forwarding is new here; the CLI already accepts claim branch and worktree.
